recipes.name: Shrimp Scampi with Linguine
recipes.summary: Shrimp in a lemon, garlic and butter sauce tossed with pasta in about 25 minutes.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water by the package directions. Save 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the shrimp with salt and pepper and cook 1 to 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque all the way through. Move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute, until fragrant but not brown.
Add the broth and lemon juice and simmer 2 minutes. Stir in the butter until melted.
Add the pasta, shrimp and parsley and toss, adding pasta water a little at a time until glossy. Serve right away.
recipes.make_ahead: Peel and devein the shrimp and slice the garlic up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: Cooked shrimp turn rubbery when frozen. Freeze raw shrimp instead.

leftovers.text: Reheat gently with a splash of water to 165°F; the shrimp may firm up a little.

recipes.kids: Leave out the pepper flakes and cut the shrimp in pieces for younger children.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 2 more tablespoons olive oil in place of the butter.

prep_day.ahead: Peel the shrimp; slice the garlic; chop the parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken, Shrimp and Sausage Jambalaya
recipes.summary: A Louisiana one-pot of rice simmered with smoked sausage, chicken thighs, shrimp and the holy trinity of onion, pepper and celery.
equipment: Dutch oven or large heavy pot with lid
steps: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage 5 minutes; move it to a plate.
Add the chicken and cook 5 minutes, until browned. Move it to the plate with the sausage. Wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion, pepper and celery 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, paprika, thyme, oregano, cayenne and salt and stir 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, rice, broth and bay leaves. Return the sausage and chicken. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer 20 minutes without stirring.
Scatter the shrimp over the rice, cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes more, until the rice is tender, the shrimp are pink and opaque and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Remove the bay leaves, stir gently and top with green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop the vegetables and cut the chicken up to 1 day ahead; keep the chicken separate.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for up to 2 months for best quality; the shrimp firm up a little. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F with a splash of broth.

recipes.kids: Use mild sausage and skip the cayenne; pass hot sauce at the table for grown-ups.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables, slice the sausage and cut the chicken.

recipes.name: Coconut Shrimp Curry
recipes.summary: A mild, creamy curry of shrimp, bell pepper and spinach in coconut milk, ready in 30 minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric and salt and stir 1 minute.
Stir in the coconut milk and tomatoes. Simmer 5 minutes to blend the flavors.
Add the shrimp and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Add the lime juice and top with cilantro. Serve with rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the sauce through step 3 up to 2 days ahead. Reheat to a simmer and add the shrimp.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce without shrimp for up to 3 months. Thaw, bring to a simmer and add raw shrimp.

leftovers.text: Reheat gently to 165°F and serve over rice.

recipes.kids: This curry is mild. Serve with extra rice and cucumber slices.

prep_day.ahead: Make the sauce; peel the shrimp.

recipes.name: Lowcountry Shrimp Boil
recipes.summary: A one-pot Southern feast of red potatoes, corn on the cob, smoked sausage and shrimp, piled on the table to share.
steps: Fill a large stockpot with the water. Add the salt, paprika, mustard, celery seed, cayenne and bay leaves. Squeeze in the lemon and drop in the halves, then add the onion and garlic. Bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and boil 12 minutes.
Add the corn and sausage and boil 8 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Add the shrimp, stir and cook 2 to 3 minutes, just until pink and opaque. Turn off the heat.
Drain in a colander or lift everything out with a slotted spoon. Pile it onto a platter and drizzle with melted butter. Set out a bowl for shells.
recipes.make_ahead: Halve the potatoes and break the corn up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: Cooked shrimp and potatoes do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Peel leftover shrimp and chop with the sausage and corn for a cold salad, or reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids love eating with their hands here. Peel the shrimp and cut the corn off the cob for younger ones.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter or use olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the potatoes, corn and sausage.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Salmon glazed with a quick homemade teriyaki sauce and roasted, served over rice with broccoli and cucumber.
steps: Start the rice. Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
In a small saucepan, whisk the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and water. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until glossy. Set half aside for serving.
Toss the broccoli with the oil and salt and spread it on one side of the sheet. Roast 8 minutes.
Set the salmon on the other side of the sheet and brush with the rest of the sauce. Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Fill bowls with rice, salmon, broccoli and cucumber. Drizzle with the saved sauce and top with sesame seeds and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the sauce and cook the rice up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze raw salmon instead; thaw overnight in the fridge before cooking.

leftovers.text: Pack cold bowls for lunch, or reheat the salmon and rice to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Check for pin bones by running a finger along the fillet. Kids often like the sweet glaze.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Make the sauce; cook the rice; cut the broccoli.

recipes.name: Salmon Cakes
recipes.summary: A pantry dinner: canned salmon mixed with crumbs, mustard and herbs, pan-fried crisp outside.

ingredients.prep: drained, skin and large bones removed

steps: Flake the salmon into a bowl. The soft bones in canned salmon are edible and add calcium; mash them in or pick them out.

Add the egg, panko, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, green onions, parsley and pepper and mix well. Shape into 8 patties about 1/2 inch thick. Chill 10 minutes if you have time; they hold together better.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the cakes 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F, since the cakes hold raw egg.
Serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the cakes up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked cakes on a tray, then bag them, for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in a 375°F oven to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Tuck a leftover cake into a bun with lettuce for lunch; reheat to 165°F or eat cold.

recipes.kids: Kids can mix and shape the cakes. Wash hands after handling the raw egg.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs or crushed gluten-free crackers.

recipes.name: New England Fish Chowder
recipes.summary: A creamy, old-fashioned chowder of tender cod, potatoes and a little bacon.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp. Lift it out, leaving the fat.
Add the butter, onion and celery and cook 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Slowly stir in the broth, then add the potatoes, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cod and simmer gently 5 to 6 minutes, until it reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Stir in the half-and-half and heat until steaming; do not boil. Remove the bay leaf and top with bacon and parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Make through step 3 up to 2 days ahead. Bring back to a simmer, then add the fish and cream.

freezer.text: Cream chowders with potatoes turn grainy when frozen.

leftovers.text: Reheat gently to 165°F without boiling, so the fish stays in pieces.

recipes.kids: Serve with oyster crackers. Check the cod for any stray bones.

swaps.gluten_free: Leave out the flour and mash a few of the cooked potato cubes into the broth to thicken it; check the broth and bacon labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the bacon; chop the vegetables; cube the potatoes and keep them in water in the fridge.

recipes.name: Cornmeal Oven-Fried Catfish
recipes.summary: Southern-style catfish with a crisp seasoned cornmeal crust, baked on a rack instead of deep-fried.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a wire rack on a baking sheet and brush the rack with a little of the oil.
Stir the buttermilk and hot sauce in a shallow dish and add the fillets, turning to coat.
In another dish, mix the cornmeal, flour, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Lift each fillet, let the extra buttermilk drip off and press it into the cornmeal on both sides. Set on the rack and drizzle with the rest of the oil. Wash your hands.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and crisp and the thickest part reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the cornmeal coating up to 1 week ahead and keep it in a jar.

freezer.text: The crust goes soft after freezing. Freeze raw fillets instead.

leftovers.text: Reheat on a rack in a 400°F oven to 165°F so the crust crisps again; or flake into tacos.

recipes.kids: Cut a fillet into strips before coating for crunchy fish fingers.

swaps.gluten_free: Use all cornmeal, or gluten-free flour, in the coating.

recipes.name: Parmesan-Crusted Tilapia
recipes.summary: Mild white fish topped with a lemony Parmesan and panko crust and baked in about 12 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment. Lay the fillets on it and pat them dry.
Season with salt and pepper and spread a thin layer of mayonnaise over the tops; it holds the crust on.
Mix the panko, Parmesan, butter, lemon juice, garlic powder, paprika and parsley and press it over the fish.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fish reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the topping up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze raw fillets instead; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Reheat in a 375°F oven to 165°F, or flake into a wrap.

recipes.kids: The cheesy crust makes this a good first fish for kids. Check for bones before serving.

recipes.name: Baked Cod with Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.summary: Cod fillets baked in a garlicky tomato sauce with olives, capers and fresh basil.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano and pepper flakes. Simmer 5 minutes.
Season the cod with salt and pepper and nestle it into the sauce. Spoon some sauce over the top.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish reaches 145°F in the thickest part and flakes easily. Scatter basil over and serve.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the sauce up to 3 days ahead; reheat it in the skillet before adding the fish.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce alone for up to 3 months. Freeze raw fillets separately.

leftovers.text: Reheat gently to 165°F and serve over pasta or rice.

recipes.kids: Scrape off the olives and capers for a kid portion if they prefer it plain.

recipes.name: Tuna Noodle Casserole
recipes.summary: A from-scratch version of the potluck classic: egg noodles, tuna and peas in a creamy mushroom sauce under crunchy crumbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish. Cook the noodles in salted boiling water 2 minutes less than the package says; drain.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 6 to 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth and milk and simmer, whisking, until thick, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the salt, pepper and cheese.
Fold in the noodles, tuna and peas and spread in the dish.
Toss the panko with the melted butter and sprinkle over. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden and the center reaches 165°F.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble without the topping up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Add the topping and bake 30 to 35 minutes, to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the unbaked casserole, without the topping, for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, top and bake to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions to 165°F with a splash of milk.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle on the crumbs. Chopped mushrooms melt into the sauce if kids are wary of them.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta, flour and crumbs, and check the broth.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the casserole and refrigerate it unbaked.

recipes.name: Open-Face Tuna Melts
recipes.summary: Tuna salad on toasted English muffins, topped with tomato and cheddar and broiled until bubbly.
steps: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, mustard, lemon juice and pepper.
Set the muffin halves cut side up on a baking sheet and broil 1 to 2 minutes, until lightly toasted.
Spread the tuna salad on the muffins, top each with a tomato slice and a slice of cheese.
Broil 2 to 4 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese melts and bubbles.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the tuna salad up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge.

freezer.text: Mayonnaise-based salads do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Keep extra tuna salad in the fridge for sandwiches within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the tuna and add the cheese. A grown-up handles the broiler.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread or English muffins.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and toast the bread instead.

recipes.name: Tuna Niçoise Salad
recipes.summary: A French composed salad of potatoes, green beans, eggs, tomatoes and tuna with a mustard vinaigrette.
steps: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water and bring to a boil. Cook 12 to 15 minutes, until tender. Add the green beans for the last 3 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, peel and quarter.
Shake the vinegar, mustard, garlic, salt, pepper and oil in a jar.
Halve the potatoes and toss them with a few spoonfuls of dressing while still warm.
Spread the lettuce on a platter. Arrange the potatoes, green beans, eggs, tuna, tomatoes and olives in groups on top. Drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the potatoes, beans and eggs and mix the dressing up to 3 days ahead; keep them separate in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Pack the parts in a lunch container with dressing on the side.

recipes.kids: Let kids build their own plate from the platter.

prep_day.ahead: Boil the potatoes, green beans and eggs; mix the dressing.
